topic: How can frequency planning address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems?
response: Frequency planning can address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems by allocating non-overlapping frequency bands for the two systems. This can be achieved by using a frequency separation of at least 20 MHz between the satellite uplink and the power line communication system, as specified in the ITU-R Recommendation M.1456.
